# Reusable task prompts
These are portable formulations of the established workflow, not a verbatim transcript of historical generation calls. Replace every placeholder with verified information. Never treat placeholder content as evidence.

## 1. Research and select
Read the complete available concept history and pending reservations. Propose [COUNT] fresh California Black Stories concepts with varied pillars, regions, eras, hooks and visual actions. Compare the underlying event/contribution, not only names, against the latest 200 prompt numbers. Report missing ledger coverage. Research selected concepts using credible source bodies; save a claim/evidence list including URLs, exact supporting excerpts, conflicts and unresolved claims. Do not draft unsupported milestones or pretend syndicated copies are independent sources. Do not advance the completed rotation or generate assets yet.

## 2. Inspect likeness reference
Inspect the attached/reference image [REFERENCE]. Verify its attribution using [RECORD URL]. Describe visible likeness cues only: facial proportions, jaw/chin, cheek structure, eye/brow shape, nose, mouth, hairline/texture/style, facial hair, apparent age and distinctive features. Distinguish observation from uncertainty caused by low resolution, angle, lighting, monochrome or later retouching. Record approximate reference date and whether it matches [SCENE YEAR / SUBJECT AGE]. Do not infer ethnicity, personality or exact skin shade from monochrome. Do not copy the reference's pose, clothing, text or background into the new scene by default.

## 3. Generate the final image prompt
Using only the verified claim set and inspected reference cues below, write ONE cinematic photorealistic scene paragraph depicting [REAL FULL NAME] in [DOCUMENTED PERIOD/LOCATION], meaningfully engaged in [HISTORICALLY PLAUSIBLE ACTION THAT CARRIES THE STORY]. Name the real subject; do not describe an actor, lookalike or anonymous substitute. Integrate [OBSERVED LIKENESS CUES] with era-appropriate age and grooming. Specify plausible clothing, tools, architecture and spatial relationships supported by research. Choose a composition distinct from neighboring batch items; protect the principal face and key hands/gesture within the final portrait crop. Describe lighting, camera viewpoint and documentary texture without implying an actual archival photograph. No invented readable signs, modern equipment, copied reference damage, or reference-pose duplication. End exactly: Optimized for 1080x1350 format.

Scene paragraph scaffold (not a factual example):
Photorealistic cinematic depiction of [NAME], [AGE/PERIOD AND VERIFIED LIKENESS CUES], actively [ACTION] in [PLACE AND YEAR/PERIOD]; [RESEARCH-SUPPORTED CLOTHING, OBJECTS, ENVIRONMENT AND SECONDARY FIGURES], framed [SHOT SIZE/ANGLE/COMPOSITION] with [LIGHTING AND TEXTURE], preserving clear facial structure and the story's key gesture with safe portrait-crop margins; [SCENE-SPECIFIC EXCLUSIONS/PRESERVATION CONSTRAINTS]. Optimized for 1080x1350 format.

## 4. Caption, hashtags and comment
Write a California Black Stories Facebook Caption of at least three paragraphs from the verified claim set. Use a concrete, scroll-stopping hook rather than generic 'hidden history' hype. Establish who/what/where and the meaningful historical contribution. Connect the documented story to identity, community or present relevance without invented causation or personal memories. Use warm authoritative proud language, readable sentences, line breaks and a few appropriate emojis (🏾 for supported human/hand emojis). End with a genuine engagement invitation. Include this audience-facing disclosure: Image generated with AI; not an archival photograph.
Do not put hashtags inside the base caption. Provide a separate Hashtags section with exactly five distinct relevant hashtags. Provide a separate First Comment of 1–2 sentences, warm fan-to-fan, with a verified memorable detail and an invitation to tag a friend or share; no hashtags. Finish with Batch progress: prompt [N]. Keep the claim-level Fact Check and source URLs outside the audience-facing copy and before these ending sections. Do not assert the image is archival or that a reconstructed moment was photographed.

## 5. Independent copy review
Compare each factual assertion in the caption, comment, narration and scene premise to the saved source bodies. Flag unsupported dates, 'first/only' claims, causal leaps and invented quotes. Confirm voice, at least three caption paragraphs, explicit AI disclosure, exactly five unique hashtags and no hashtags in First Comment. Check combined outgoing payload for duplicate hashtag blocks. Preserve approved wording; propose material corrections for renewed approval.

## 6. Visual review
Open both the inspected likeness reference and the actual final generated image. Apply LIKENESS_QA.md. Report observations and uncertainty, not invented confidence percentages. Inspect the decoded final crop, not just a source thumbnail. If the image fails, identify the specific fix, preserve version history and regenerate only within authorized scope. If likeness evidence is inadequate, mark unresolved rather than calling it approved.

## 7. Motion-only prompt
From the approved source still [ASSET VERSION/HASH], describe [SUBTLE PLAUSIBLE SUBJECT MOVEMENT], [CAMERA MOVEMENT], and [AMBIENT MOVEMENT]. Preserve the source face/identity, apparent age, hairstyle, clothing, tools, architecture, era and composition. Do not introduce identifiable people, new props, readable invented signs, modern objects, face morphing, excessive gestures or camera moves revealing unsupported geometry. Use restrained documentary motion unless a different style was explicitly approved. This prompt does not authorize animation dispatch.

## 8. Final review request
Present version [VERSION], prompt numbers [EXACT SET], all final assets, exact captions/hashtags/comments, fact-check URLs and remaining QA caveats. State what has and has not been generated, assembled, uploaded, scheduled or verified. Ask approval for a clearly bounded next action. For scheduling/publication specify exact destination/page, calendar date, time and time zone, and the exact finalized package. Do not reuse approvals for prior versions or other actions.
